item.title: Houthis threaten "painful" response if U.S. joins Saudi offensive
item.description: As Trump mulls joining Saudi Arabia in attacking the Houthis, the Iran-backed group is threatening a "painful" response.

item.title: Six Flags stock slides 16% following fatal roller coaster accident
item.description: The company's stock is taking a hit after officials confirmed a person died at one of the theme park's locations, extending a slide that started in September.

item.title: Lesser-known menopause symptoms to look out for
item.description: Pilar Guzman, the editorial director at Oprah Daily, and Dr. Sharon Malone, a board-certified OBGYN, sit down with "CBS Mornings" to discuss ways that women and their partners can better manage menopause symptoms. They both contributed to the new book, "The Book of Menopause: Real Talk, Real Science, Real Strategies for Your Next Chapter."

item.title: Spectacular launch sends cargo ship on voyage to space station
item.description: Along with crew supplies and equipment, the Cargo Dragon is delivering two rollout solar arrays to complete a major power system upgrade.

item.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle ousted as ambassador over corruption allegations
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle said she is stepping aside as U.S. ambassador to Greece, days after reports that she offered access to officials in exchange for help paying off her debt.

item.title: Friend of woman allegedly killed by officer says suicide claim "a lie"
item.description: Lauren Andrews says she spoke with Sandra Birchmore just two weeks before her death and never believed the medical examiner's initial conclusion that Birchmore died by suicide.

item.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle is preparing to resign
item.description: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle is preparing to resign after she allegedly asked a Trump donor to pay off her credit card bill in exchange for political access. CBS News' Natalie Brand reports.

item.title: Russia strikes Ukrainian targets despite Trump's energy ceasefire claims
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says that Russia has struck at least six energy facilities despite President Trump's claims of an "energy ceasefire." CBS News' Aidan Stretch reports.

item.title: Why an Iowa farmers union endorsed 18 Democratic candidates
item.description: A bipartisan farmers union in Iowa endorsed 18 Democratic candidates in the upcoming midterm elections. CBS News' Lana Zak has more context.

item.title: Hurricane Simon hits Mexico after storms kill 5
item.description: Hurricane Simon continued to move slowly up the coast of west-central Mexico after tropical weather systems caused five deaths and damage in Pacific coastal towns and resorts.

item.title: Six Flags closes 9 rides across 6 parks after deadly incident
item.description: Six Flags has temporarily closed rides similar to Goliath, the roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia that a man fell from.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Mark Harmon and Austin Stowell on playing different eras of "NCIS" character Leroy Jethro Gibbs
item.description: In the latest installment of "Between Us," actors Mark Harmon and Austin Stowell sit down to talk about portraying the iconic "NCIS" character Leroy Jethro Gibbs in different eras.

item.title: How Iran made the Houthis into such a problem
item.description: 10 years ago, few people had heard of the Houthis. Here's how the Yemeni rebels have become Iran's "most powerful proxy."

item.title: Tributes pour in for "Breaking Bad" star RJ Mitte
item.description: Tributes are pouring in for RJ Mitte, who starred in "Breaking Bad" as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr., after his sudden death at age 34.

item.title: Oprah's Book Club pick Amanda Rizkalla reads "Hungered" excerpt
item.description: Oprah Winfrey selected "Hungered" by debut novelist Amanda Rizkalla as her latest book club pick. Watch the author, Amanda Rizkalla, read an excerpt from her novel that Oprah says "compassionately tackles the difficult subject of families who live outside the margins."

item.title: Ashe on why "Stop The Wedding" is the first single off her new album
item.description: Ashe talks to Anthony Mason about her fourth solo album, "The Girl of Your Dreams," working with Finneas and finding empathy for herself.

item.title: Character.ai declares bankruptcy, citing legal and business woes
item.description: AI company has faced multiple lawsuits from families who claimed their teenage children died by suicide or harmed themselves after using its platform.

item.title: Is a bootleg weight-loss drug to blame for 2 reported deaths?
item.description: While unverified, the reports come amid growing efforts to clamp down on illicit sales of the experimental weight-loss drug retatrutide.

item.title: Questions arise after 2 people die using black-market weight-loss drug
item.description: Two deaths were reported to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration that may be tied to the use of bootleg weight-loss drugs, documents reviewed by CBS News show.

item.title: Texas Democratic Party leader on tight Senate race between Talarico and Paxton
item.description: Texas Democratic Party chair Kendall Scudder joins CBS News with more on the Senate race between James Talarico and Ken Paxton.

item.title: White House asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign, Trump's new press secretary Katie Zacharia says
item.description: President Trump's new press secretary, Katie Zacharia, said that the White House has asked U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports on Zacharia's first briefing.

item.title: Stunning details emerge in case of cop accused of raping, killing Sandra Birchmore
item.description: More details are emerging on Matthew Farwell, a former Massachusetts police officer accused of raping and killing Sandra Birchmore, who he had an alleged sexual relationship with for years prior. Tom Hanson spoke with the mother of one of Birchmore's closest friends to learn more.

item.title: Mars rover sets new driving record on surface of another world
item.description: NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has set a new record for the longest distance traveled on the surface of another planet, the space agency said.

item.title: Selma Blair arrested after allegedly biting flight attendant
item.description: Actress Selma Blair was arrested after an incident on board a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to John F. Kennedy International Airport Sunday night.

item.title: Talarico was home in Texas during campaign absence, photos indicate
item.description: James Talarico's campaign shared security camera footage with CBS News that appears to show him at his home in Texas for the first eight days of this month — pushing back on claims that Talarico was hiding the reasons for his disappearance.

item.title: RJ Mitte, "Breaking Bad" actor, dies at 34
item.description: RJ Mitte rose to fame playing Walter White Jr. on the hit series "Breaking Bad."

item.title: Data center boom puts GOP in a bind before midterms
item.description: Cleanview Research found 75% of data centers being built and 80% of data centers in the planning stage are in predominantly GOP states, as public opposition to data centers grows.

item.title: Zelenskyy says Russia isn't honoring Trump's energy ceasefire
item.description: Within a day of President Trump announcing an "energy ceasefire," Ukraine said Russia had struck a power plant and other energy facilities across the country.

item.title: Nobel Prize in economics goes to 2 Americans
item.description: American-born economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford won the Nobel Prize in economics for their work on models that help governments and central banks manage economic shocks.
